summary:
It looks like you've successfully deleted all the prefetch files in your Windows system. Prefetch files are used by Windows to improve boot time by storing information about which applications are likely to be run next, and then loading them into memory when the computer boots.

If you're running this on a production system, it's recommended to ensure that there are no other critical processes or applications being used before deleting these files. Additionally, if there were any important data stored in prefetches (which is very unlikely), those data would be lost as well.

For future reference, if you want to prevent Windows from creating prefetch files again, you can set the "Create Prefetch Files" option in the Power Plan settings to "Disabled". This will stop the creation of these files on boot.
